name: Onboarding
notes:
# Onboarding

## Purpose

Onboard a network device into Nautobot from nothing but an IP address (or
`name,ip_address`) typed at run start — no saved inventory, no prior Nautobot
record required. Discovers the device's real hostname and serial number live
from the device itself, sets default Nautobot attributes (role, location,
device type, secrets_groups, a serial placeholder) centrally before creation, derives its interfaces via Batfish,
turns the hostname into an FQDN by appending the device's domain name, then creates it in Nautobot and
starts the Nautobot job "Sync Network Data From Network".
Reach for this workflow specifically when onboarding a device Nautobot
doesn't know about yet; for a device already in Nautobot, a plain
`Get from Nautobot` → `Update Nautobot Device` workflow is simpler and
doesn't need any of the live-discovery machinery below.

## Assumptions / prerequisites

- `Get Configs`/`Run Command` use the `cisco - noc` credential (fixed,
  `credential_source: "fixed"`) — the run fails immediately if that
  credential no longer resolves.
- `Init Batfish Snapshot`/`Extract Facts` use the `batfish` source; `Add to
  Nautobot`/`Start Job` use the `nautobot` source. Both must resolve in
  Settings → Sources.
- `Start Job` runs the Nautobot job `Sync Network Data From Network` (a Nautobot
  onboarding-plugin job) with `namespace: Global`, all three statuses `Active`,
  and `devices: {nautobot.id}`. That namespace and those status names must
  exist in Nautobot (they are resolved to UUIDs at run time).
- The device's domain name must be present in its running config (an `ip domain
  name ...` line), because `Append domain to Devicename` reads it from
  `parsed.cisco_config.running.identity.domain_name`.
- **Nautobot device defaults (role, location, device type, secrets_groups, serial
  placeholder) live in one place: `Set Default Attributes`'s config, inside
  the `Set Nautobot Attributes` group — not in `Add to Nautobot` anymore.**
  `Add to Nautobot`'s `device_fields` (`role`, `status`, `location`,
  `device_type`, `platform`, `software_version`, `secrets_groups`, `serial`, 
  `asset_tag`, `tags`) are all `{nautobot.origin}` expressions now, reading 
  whatever is in each device's `attribute_bags.nautobot` at that point in the run. 
  Cloning this workflow for a different site/role/model means editing
  `Set Default Attributes`'s config (currently `role: "Network"`,
  `location: "City A"`, `device_type: {model: "networkA", manufacturer:
  "Cisco"}`), not hunting through `Add to Nautobot`'s fields.
- Only Cisco IOS/IOS-XE is exercised (`network_driver_override: "cisco_ios"`
  on both `Parse Cisco Config` and `Run Command`) — `show version`'s TextFSM
  template and `parse-cisco-config`'s parser are both IOS-specific.
- `Get from User`'s `lookup_mode` is `"manual"` — the operator types the IP
  (or `name,ip_address`) with no Nautobot-backed suggestions. Fan-out is
  disabled: this workflow onboards one device per run, not a batch.

## Gotchas

- **The `Funnel` node feeding `Set Default Attributes` is purely cosmetic —
  it does nothing at run time.** `funnel`'s registry entry
  (`registry.yaml`) is `executable: false`: "each incoming edge is resolved
  directly between its real source and the funnel's one destination before
  execution." So `Set Default Attributes` is the *real* join point for the
  two parallel branches (`Get Configs`→`Parse Cisco Config`, and
  `Run Command`) — it receives one device context with both branches'
  results already merged (same join semantics as any other multi-parent
  node), the Funnel just tidies up the canvas. Don't read it as a step that
  runs or changes anything.
- **`device.name` starts as the raw typed value (often just the IP) and must
  be renamed to the device's real hostname before Batfish ever runs — this
  is why `Set device name and serial number` (inside the `Set Nautobot
  Attributes` group) sits between the join and Fan In, not after.**
  `Get from User` sets `device.name` to whatever the operator typed (an IP,
  if no name was given). `Batfish Extract Facts` defaults its node filter to
  `device.name.lower()` *and* attributes facts back to devices by that same
  lowercased name — but Batfish's own node name always comes from the
  `hostname` line inside the actual parsed config, not from anything Manus
  knows beforehand. A bare IP address isn't even valid Batfish
  node-specifier syntax (a literal 400 from the Batfish API), and even a
  valid-looking name wouldn't match. `Set device name and serial number`'s
  first entry fixes this by copying
  `parsed.cisco_config.running.hostname` → `device.name` before Fan
  In/Batfish Init Snapshot run. The rename also means `Add to Nautobot`
  creates the device under its real name instead of the typed IP (the FQDN
  suffix is added later, see the next point).
- **`Append domain to Devicename` (`update-attribute`, `template` mode) must
  stay *after* `Config to Attributes`, i.e. after Batfish — do not move it up
  next to `Set device name and serial number`.** It turns `device.name` from
  the short hostname into `<hostname>.<domain>` (e.g. `LAB` → `LAB.local.zz`).
  Batfish's node name comes from the `hostname` line of the config (the short
  name), and `Extract Facts` attributes facts back to devices by that name
  (see above), so renaming to the FQDN before Batfish would make the facts
  stop matching the device. It has to be the last rename before `Add to
  Nautobot`, whose `name` field is `{device.name}`.
  - It uses `template` mode with `template:
    "{device.name}.{parsed.cisco_config.running.identity.domain_name}"`, not
    `regex` mode. A regex `destination_template` only understands
    backreferences (`\1`) of the *source* value, so `{device.name}` in it
    would be written literally into the name. `template` mode is the one mode
    that can combine several attributes, including the destination's own
    current value.
  - The domain comes from `Parse Cisco Config`'s output (the running config),
    not from Batfish, even though it is applied after Batfish runs.
  - **If the config has no domain name, the step is silently skipped** (a
    `template` update is skipped for a device when any `{placeholder}` can't
    be resolved — no exception, no failure outcome), and the device is
    created in Nautobot with its short hostname. Same "quiet no-op" failure
    mode as the serial extraction below; check the `ip domain name` line in
    the config first if a device shows up without its FQDN.
- **`Run Command`'s TextFSM output is always a list, even for a single-row
  command like `show version` — and ntc-templates declares `serial`,
  `hardware`, and `mac_address` as `List` fields, so they're a list *inside*
  that one row too.** The real shape is
  `parsed.parsed["show version"].parsed` = `[{"hostname": "...", "serial":
  ["FCW2148XXXX"], ...}]`. Reaching the serial number needs a **literal
  positional index**, not a filter (there's no per-device field known ahead
  of time to filter on anyway, and a multi-item list would be genuinely
  ambiguous): `Set device name and serial number`'s second entry uses
  `source_path: "parsed.parsed.show version.parsed[0].serial"`, writing to
  **`nautobot.serial`** (not `custom.serial` — it has to land in the
  `nautobot` bag for `Add to Nautobot`'s `{nautobot.origin}` field to pick
  it up at all). Two syntax traps found live building this: (1) `show
  version` is a fine plain path segment as-is — only a literal `.` splits
  segments, spaces don't need quoting or bracketing (`parsed["show
  version"]` looks natural but is wrong — it's treated as one literal,
  nonexistent dict key and silently resolves to nothing, no error); (2) the
  bracket form is `[0]` (a bare digit), not `[]` — an empty bracket isn't
  recognized at all. A wrong `source_path` here fails **silently** —
  `Update Attribute` just skips that device for that one attribute (no
  exception, no failure outcome) — which is exactly why `Set Default
  Attributes` seeds `nautobot.serial = "unknown"` as a placeholder *before*
  this step runs: if the regex ever stops matching, the device still gets
  created with a visible, obviously-fake serial instead of a blank/missing
  one, and it's a cheap tell that this extraction broke — check this path
  first if a device's serial in Nautobot ever reads "unknown".
- **`Set Location` (the group's exit node) only fires for hostnames matching
  `^R(\d+)\w+.*$`.** For any hostname that doesn't match — including
  `LAB`, the worked example below — it's a silent no-op (same "regex
  doesn't match → skip, no error" behavior as above), leaving `Set Default
  Attributes`'s `location: "City A"` default untouched. When it *does*
  match, it overwrites `nautobot.location` with just the captured digit
  group (e.g. hostname `R42-SW1` → `nautobot.location = "42"`) — that's
  almost certainly not a real Nautobot location name, so if a future device
  onboarded through this workflow has an `R<digits>...`-shaped hostname,
  double-check what `Add to Nautobot`'s location resolution actually does
  with it before trusting the result.
- **`Add to Nautobot` creates the device including all interfaces
  (`interfaces_source: "nautobot_origin"`, i.e. the `nautobot.interfaces` bag
  `Config to Attributes` built) and, because `refresh_attributes_after_create`
  is on, reloads the device from Nautobot to get its real UUID.** `Start Job`
  passes that UUID (`devices: {nautobot.id}`) to `Sync Network Data From
  Network`, so the job syncs exactly this one device. Turning the refresh off
  would leave `{nautobot.id}` empty and the job would have no device to work on.
- **An already-existing device is not handled by this workflow.** `Add to
  Nautobot` fails such a device with error code `device_already_exists` on its
  `failure` outcome, and nothing is wired to that outcome, so `Start Job` never
  runs for it. The earlier `Update Device` path is gone; use a `Get from
  Nautobot` → `Update Nautobot Device` workflow for devices Nautobot already
  knows.
- **Batfish is used only to derive interfaces here, not for any routing/ACL
  query** — `Config to Attributes` (`source_format: "batfish"`) reads
  `Extract Facts`' output solely to build the `nautobot.interfaces` bag for
  the Nautobot write. `network_name` is left at the default
  (`manus-workflow-29`), and `retain_snapshots` is unset — nothing prunes old
  snapshots for this workflow, so its Batfish network accumulates one
  snapshot per run indefinitely.

## Example

Operator enters `192.168.178.240` (no name) when starting the run.
`Get from User` → `device.name = "192.168.178.240"` (the typed value).
Parallel: `Get Configs` fetches the running config → `Parse Cisco Config`
reads it (config source `running`); `Run Command` runs `show version`
(TextFSM). Both join at `Set Default Attributes` (the `Funnel` feeding it is
cosmetic — see Gotchas), which seeds `nautobot.role = "Network"`,
`nautobot.location = "City A"`, `nautobot.device_type = {model: "networkA",
manufacturer: "Cisco"}`, and `nautobot.serial = "unknown"` (a bag that was
empty until now, so every enabled default lands). `Set device name and
serial number` renames `device.name → "LAB"` (the device's real configured
hostname) and overwrites `nautobot.serial = "FCW2148XXXX"` (the real
extracted value, replacing the placeholder). `Set Location` checks `"LAB"`
against `^R(\d+)\w+.*$` — no match, so it's a no-op and
`nautobot.location` stays `"City A"`. `Fan In` → `Init Batfish Snapshot`
(network `manus-workflow-29`, snapshot `run-<run id>`) → `Extract Facts` →
`Config to Attributes` derives interfaces (with `update_primary_ipv4`
matching `Ethernet`/`Vlan` interfaces) into `nautobot.interfaces`. The running
config contains `ip domain name local.zz`, so `Append domain to Devicename`
renames `device.name` from `"LAB"` to `"LAB.local.zz"` (Batfish has already
run, so the short name it knew is no longer needed). `Add to Nautobot` then
creates device `LAB.local.zz` (role `Network`, location `City A`, device type
`networkA`/Cisco, serial `FCW2148XXXX`, and all interfaces) and reloads it to
get its Nautobot UUID. Because the device did not exist yet, `Add to Nautobot`
succeeds and `Start Job` starts the Nautobot job `Sync Network Data From
Network` for that UUID (`namespace: Global`, statuses `Active`, VLAN/VRF/cable/
software-version sync enabled). If the device had already existed, `Add to
Nautobot` would fail it with `device_already_exists` and the run would end
there without starting the job.

data.title: Init Batfish Snapshot
data.overview: Build a Batfish snapshot from this run's device configs.
data.description: Assembles the current run's device running-configs into a fresh Batfish snapshot and records its location for downstream Batfish query steps (Routing Table, Path Check, ACL Check). Not fan-out-safe -- like store-artifact/git steps, this must run after a Fan In in a fanned-out workflow, never inside the fanned-out branch (see doc/BATFISH_INTEGRATION.md "Snapshot lifecycle").

data.title: Get Configs
data.overview: Get device configuration in the chosen format.
data.description: Get device configuration in the specified format.

data.title: Extract Facts
data.overview: Pull parsed device facts out of a Batfish snapshot via Batfish's extract_facts question.
data.description: Retrieves the configuration facts Batfish parsed (hostname, NTP/ TACACS/DNS servers, interfaces, BGP/OSPF settings, etc.) for a set of nodes in an already-initialized snapshot -- no expected values, just what Batfish actually sees. Writes each device's own facts into device.parsed[output_key] for downstream steps to read, in addition to one workflow-level artifact covering every extracted node.

data.title: Config to Attributes
data.overview: Turn parsed device config into Nautobot attributes.
data.description: Read a device's parsed config — from Parse Cisco Config or Get & Parse Config (pyATS/Genie) — and populate its Nautobot attribute bag, starting with Layer3 interfaces, for later use by Add to Nautobot or Update Device (interfaces_source: nautobot_origin). A Batfish source_format is planned as a future addition to this same contract. No live Nautobot connection is used.

data.title: Fan In
data.overview: Rejoin fan-out branches into one execution path.
data.description: Rejoin a fanned-out workflow into a single path. Per-device steps run in parallel child workflows up to this node; steps placed after it run once over all devices. Place git / store-artifact steps after Fan In for safe, single-commit exports.

data.title: Get from User
data.overview: Ask the operator for devices when the run starts.
data.description: Prompt the operator to enter one or more target devices when starting the workflow run.

data.title: Add to Nautobot
data.overview: Create a new device in Nautobot.
data.description: Create each device in Nautobot with its required attributes, plus optional interfaces, rack placement, and virtual chassis membership.

data.title: Parse Cisco Config
data.overview: Parse a Cisco running/startup config into structured data.
data.description: Parse a Cisco IOS/IOS-XE/NXOS/XR running and/or startup configuration into structured data (hostname, VRFs, VLANs, interfaces, ACLs, routing, etc.) using cisco-config-parser, for use by Jinja templates and Log Attributes.

data.overview: Set or transform device attributes in the workflow.
data.description: Set or transform one or more in-workflow device attributes using a fixed value or a regular expression with capture groups.

data.title: Run Command
data.overview: Execute CLI commands on connected devices.
data.description: Execute one or more CLI commands on connected devices.

data.title: Set Location
data.overview: Set or transform device attributes in the workflow.
data.description: Set or transform one or more in-workflow device attributes using a fixed value or a regular expression with capture groups.

data.title: Funnel
data.overview: Merge many connections into one before a shared destination.
data.description: Canvas decoration — accepts edges from many upstream steps and routes them through a single downstream connection, reducing visual clutter for fan-in patterns like Notify On Error. Not executed at runtime; each incoming edge is resolved directly between its real source and the funnel's one destination before execution.

data.title: Set Default Attributes
data.overview: Seed default Nautobot attributes for devices that don't have them yet.
data.description: Fill in default role/status/location/device type/tags/custom fields/interfaces into each device's Nautobot attribute bag, so {nautobot.origin} in Add to Nautobot / Update Device resolves without a live Nautobot lookup.

data.title: Background
data.overview: Place a colored rectangle behind other canvas steps.
data.description: Canvas decoration — a colored rectangle always drawn behind other steps. Configure size and color. Not executed at runtime and cannot be connected to other steps.

data.title: Label
data.overview: Place styled text on the workflow canvas.
data.description: Canvas decoration — configurable text with size, font, and color. Not executed at runtime and cannot be connected to other steps.

job_variables_schema.name: sync_vrf_to_prefix
job_variables_schema.help_text: Associate each interface's VRF with the parent prefix of the interface's IP addresses. Requires 'Sync VRFs'. Associations are add-only; stale prefix/VRF links are not removed.

job_variables_schema.help_text: Sync cables between interfaces via a LLDP or CDP.

job_variables_schema.name: sync_software_version
job_variables_schema.help_text: Sync software version from device.

job_variables_schema.name: update_devices_with_changed_serial
job_variables_schema.help_text: If a device at the specified location already exists in Nautobot but the serial number reported by the device differs from the stored serial (e.g. after a stack master role flip or hardware swap), include this device in the sync anyway. Without this flag the device is excluded from `devices_to_load` because the queryset filter requires both name and serial to match.

job_variables_schema.help_text: The namespace for all IP addresses created or updated in the sync.

job_variables_schema.help_text: Status to be applied to all synced device interfaces. This will update existing interface statuses.

job_variables_schema.help_text: Status to be applied to all new created prefixes. Prefix status does not update with additional syncs.

job_variables_schema.help_text: Only update devices at a specific location.

job_variables_schema.help_text: Only update devices with the selected role.
